summary: Payments are failing because the outbound mTLS client certificate (CN=payments-client.orangeinvest.internal) that payment-service uses to call bank-partner-api expired at 2026-04-02T12:15:00Z and was not rotated; from 12:15:27Z every handshake is rejected with 'tls: expired certificate (alert 45)'. Confidence is high (H1 at 0.90, all alternatives rejected at ≤0.06). The HTTP error-rate panel stays green because payment-service records these as business-level PENDING_RETRY, not HTTP 5xx: error_rate is flat at ~0.2% while bank_api_error_rate hits 100% and payment_success_rate collapses to ~2.5%. The failure was predicted by the cert-watcher 25 minutes in advance and is independent of the only deployment (settlement dep-5510) and config change (bank.api.timeout_ms) in the window.

ranked_hypotheses.title: Client mTLS certificate for payment-service → bank-partner-api expired at 12:15Z
ranked_hypotheses.statement: The outbound mTLS client certificate CN=payments-client.orangeinvest.internal used by payment-service to call bank-partner-api reached its notAfter=2026-04-02T12:15:00Z and was not rotated. From 12:15:27Z every handshake is rejected by the bank gateway with 'tls: expired certificate (alert 45)'; payment-service marks affected transfers PENDING_RETRY at business level without emitting HTTP errors, so transfers fail (100% bank_api_error_rate, ~2.5% success) while the HTTP error-rate panel stays green.

causal_chain.claim: payment-service's client cert CN=payments-client.orangeinvest.internal has a hard notAfter=2026-04-02T12:15:00Z (a fixed, schedulable property, not caused by any change in the window)
cert-watcher logs a WARN 25 min before expiry (11:50:26Z) naming the exact notAfter, giving an independent timeline
At/after 12:15:00Z the cert expires; first TLS expiry ERROR at 12:15:27Z and continuing through 13:58:39Z
bank-partner-api rejects the mTLS handshake: 'remote error: tls: expired certificate (alert 45)'
payment-service records the failure as a business-level PENDING_RETRY rather than an HTTP 5xx, so the HTTP error_rate panel does not move
Resulting user-visible payment failures: bank_api_error_rate 0.2% -> 83-100% from the 12:14Z bucket; payment_success_rate ~99% -> 2.4-2.7%
The failure is on the only anomalous dependency path (bank-partner-api, observed solely via payment-service); all other neighbors (ledger-db, kafka) show no coincident anomaly

assumptions: The bank gateway is the party enforcing client-cert validity and returning alert 45 (strongly supported by F2 wording, but the bank side has no telemetry to confirm independently).
No prior renewal/config change was scheduled that should have rotated this cert before 12:15Z (cert-watcher fired, so no rotation was in flight).

ranked_hypotheses.title: Bank/acquirer side (external) failure causing the rejections
ranked_hypotheses.statement: The reporter's alternative suspicion: the failure originates on the bank/acquirer side (external provider degrading), not in our platform. Partially true in that the rejection happens at the bank end, but the origin is our own expired client cert, so this is a symptom-side attribution rather than the root cause.

causal_chain.claim: bank-partner-api is an external dependency with no telemetry, observable only via payment-service
payment-service calls to the bank fail and customers report transfer failures
The bank side is degraded/changed and rejecting our calls

assumptions: That the bank independently changed behavior at 12:15Z, coincident with our cert expiry (an improbable coincidence).
ranked_hypotheses.rejection_reason: The error text is explicit and self-incriminating: 'our client cert ... notAfter=2026-04-02T12:15:00Z' (F2), independently predicted by cert-watcher 25 min earlier (F14). The bank is the party enforcing the check, but the fault originates in our expired certificate, not bank degradation; no bank-side change is evidenced (F19).

ranked_hypotheses.title: settlement-service dep-5510 CSV-exporter deploy degraded shared ledger-db, causing payment failures
ranked_hypotheses.statement: The orchestrator's top suspect: settlement-service v1.9.0 'new CSV exporter' (dep-5510, 10:30Z) wrote to the shared ledger-db, whose degradation then broke payment-service's transfer writes. This is supported by topology (ledger-db shared by four services, F12) and a historical precedent pattern (HIST-111, F13), but the direct telemetry contradicts it.

causal_chain.claim: settlement-service v1.9.0 CSV-exporter (dep-5510) deployed 10:30Z, the only deploy in the window
ledger-db is shared by order/portfolio/payment/settlement services, so a settlement-side write pattern reaches a datastore payment-service uses
The new exporter ran full/heavy scans and degraded ledger-db (historical analogue HIST-111)
Degraded ledger-db caused payment-service transfers to fail
Users see payment failures and a green HTTP panel

assumptions: That ledger-db (which emits no logs and no latency_p99 metric) degraded at 12:15Z despite flat cpu/lag/connections.
That the new exporter generates heavy queries immediately and continuously from 10:30Z.
ranked_hypotheses.rejection_reason: Direct evidence contradicts it: ledger-db cpu_pct, replication_lag_ms and connections_active are flat with no 12:15Z anomaly (F15, F17); the slow-query blip peaks ~12:00Z and is back to baseline by 12:10Z, ~15-20 min BEFORE onset (F16); settlement-service emitted ZERO errors 10:30-12:30Z (F18); and the actual failure signature is a TLS cert expiry, unrelated to datastore latency (F2, F19). A ~105-minute quiet gap between deploy and onset also contradicts causation.

ranked_hypotheses.title: bank.api.timeout_ms config change (3000->5000 at 11:20Z) caused/coincided with the failure
ranked_hypotheses.statement: The only config change in the window (F9: bank.api.timeout_ms raised to 5000ms at 11:20Z, 'after partner advisory') is a candidate cause: a longer timeout could delay error surfacing or alter handshake behavior, and the reporter/orchestrator flagged a possible config origin. On inspection this is a weak lead.

causal_chain.claim: This changed the outbound bank-call behavior and led to the reported transfer failures
Failures appear ~55 min later at 12:15Z with a TLS cert-expiry signature

assumptions: That a timeout change could produce a TLS expired-certificate alert (no plausible mechanism; F2 shows a fixed notAfter).
ranked_hypotheses.rejection_reason: No mechanism: an HTTP/socket timeout change cannot expire or reject a client certificate. The failure is a hard TLS alert 45 with a fixed notAfter=12:15:00Z (F2, F14) that is independent of timing (F14). The change at 11:20Z precedes onset by ~55 min and shows no alignment with the 12:15Z cert expiry; F19 explicitly ties no change to the cert expiry.

recommended_actions.action: Mitigate now: rotate/renew the payment-service client certificate CN=payments-client.orangeinvest.internal and reload it into payment-service's outbound TLS config (and restart/reload the pod so the new cert is picked up), then confirm handshakes to bank-partner-api succeed again.
recommended_actions.rationale: The failure is a hard TLS alert 45 on a certificate whose notAfter=2026-04-02T12:15:00Z has passed; restoring a valid client cert is the only fix that addresses the observed error signature.

recommended_actions.action: After rotation, replay the PENDING_RETRY transfers (the 140 PENDING_RETRY records logged between 12:15:27Z and 13:58:39Z) and verify payment_success_rate returns to ~99% and bank_api_error_rate to baseline.
recommended_actions.rationale: Transfers were parked at business level, not failed with HTTP 5xx, so customer impact persists until retries succeed; success-rate recovery is the verification signal.

recommended_actions.action: Add/extend a business-level alert on payment-service bank_api_error_rate and payment_success_rate (and on PENDING_RETRY rate), so a green HTTP error_rate panel can no longer mask functional payment failures.
recommended_actions.rationale: HTTP error_rate stayed 0.16-0.26% while bank_api_error_rate hit 100% and success rate fell to ~2.5%, which is why the incident was only found via tickets.

recommended_actions.action: Verify the cert-watcher path end-to-end: confirm the 11:50:26Z WARN was delivered and ticketed, and that automatic renewal/rotation actively re-issues and hot-reloads client certs with enough lead time (not merely warning).
recommended_actions.rationale: The expiry was predicted 25 minutes in advance but the cert was not rotated, so detection existed without remediation.

recommended_actions.action: Close out the rejected leads explicitly: confirm no relation between dep-5510 (settlement CSV exporter) and ledger-db health (cpu/lag/connections flat, slow-query blip pre-onset) and note that the bank.api.timeout_ms 3000->5000 change at 11:20Z is unrelated to cert expiry — do not roll back either change on this basis alone.
recommended_actions.rationale: The only deploy and only config change in the window are affirmatively contradicted as causes; rolling them back would add risk without addressing the failure.

recommended_actions.action: Add a pre-expiry rotation gate/policy for all outbound mTLS client certs: enforce automated rotation well before notAfter with hard fail rather than WARN, plus expiry monitoring across every service-to-partner credential.
recommended_actions.rationale: The root cause is a missing rotation of a schedulable, known-expiry credential; the same class of failure can recur on any other partner integration.

recommended_actions.action: Improve observability of the bank path: surface bank-partner-api call outcomes (success/error/retry rates, TLS handshake failures) as first-class dashboards/alerts, and capture the bank gateway's own response/telemetry where the contract allows.
recommended_actions.rationale: bank-partner-api has has_telemetry:false and is only observable through payment-service, which delayed independent confirmation and forces reliance on caller-side logs.

data_gaps: bank-partner-api has no logs or metrics (has_telemetry:false), so the bank/acquirer side of the mTLS rejection could not be inspected directly; only the caller's view is available.

bank-partner-api is external with no telemetry and no outbound bank-call trace query was run, so it cannot be determined whether the bank gateway contributed anything beyond enforcing cert validity, nor whether the 5000ms timeout change was a reaction or a cause.

Within the 12:14Z bucket, bank_api_error_rate already averaged 83.37% (max 100) and success rate 18.65%, but 360s bucket granularity prevents pinning the exact second of transition; the log-based 12:15:27Z onset is the tightest bound obtained.

ledger-db exposes no latency_p99_ms metric and emits no logs; it was excluded as a cause mainly via flat cpu_pct/replication_lag_ms/connections_active and the pre-onset slow-query blip rather than a negative latency measurement, and disk_used_pct was not queried.

No payment-service latency/queue-depth/pending-transfer metrics were retrieved, so the precise mechanism by which failures stay invisible to the HTTP error-rate panel is inferred (business-level PENDING_RETRY) rather than directly measured.

Deployment/config listings for payment-adjacent services (transfer/ledger workers, kafka, api-gateway) were not individually queried; only the unscoped all-services call was used, so a change in a worker service could have been missed if that listing is filtered or capped.
api-gateway WARN/ERROR query for 12:00-13:59Z returned zero matches, leaving it unverified whether the anomaly surfaces in neighbouring services.

No config/service inventory for cert-watcher was retrieved, so it could not be definitively ruled out that a config change altered a cert renewal path before the 12:15Z expiry (though no such change appears in the 10:00-13:00Z change set).

Tool reliability: query_logs(service=bank-partner-api) and query_metrics(metric=latency_p99_ms, service=ledger-db) both FAILED with not_found, capping the direct evidence available for those components.
what_would_change_the_conclusion: Evidence that the client certificate CN=payments-client.orangeinvest.internal was actually valid (or was successfully renewed and reloaded) at or after 2026-04-02T12:15:00Z — e.g. a rotation/reload record — which would break the direct causal link between the notAfter and the onset.

Evidence that bank-partner-api independently changed behaviour at ~12:15Z (e.g. bank-side advisory, gateway config change, or its own error telemetry) coincident with our cert expiry, which would resurrect the external-dependency hypothesis H4.

Telemetry showing ledger-db degradation at 12:15Z (e.g. a latency or lock/contention spike, or a disk_used_pct anomaly) coinciding with onset, which would revive the shared-datastore hypothesis H3 despite the flat cpu/lag/connections and pre-onset slow-query blip.

Discovery of an additional change (a service, config, or certificate-rotation path) in the 10:00-13:00Z window that was not returned by the unscoped deployment/config listing, which could indicate a missed trigger.

Evidence that the TLS alert-45 handshake failures are being raised or reported by a different client identity/channel than the one whose expiry F14 predicted, which would mean the attached certificate path is not the one in failure.
